children: Shares of IFCI and New India Assurance Company rose up to 15 percent on Friday following a report that the National Stock Exchange (NSE) is targeting a listing on September 25.
The sharp rise in the two stocks came after CNBC-TV18 reported that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is likely to approve NSE's initial public offering (IPO) next week.
According to the report, NSE is likely to file an updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI next week following the approval.
The exchange is also likely to announce the price band for its IPO on September 11, the report said.
CNBC-TV18 reported that NSE is targeting a listing on September 25. It also said it had written to SEBI and was awaiting a response.
Shares of IFCI rose 11.51 percent to Rs 106.95 per share on the NSE, at around 12 p.m.

The sharp uptick was seen as the company, a public sector non-banking financial company (NBFC), holds a 52 percent stake in Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd (SHCIL), which in turn owns a 4.4 percent stake in the NSE.
The same momentum was witnessed in shares of New India Assurance Company, which rose to Rs 224.41, marking a 14.89 percent gain.
Investor interest in the stock was seen as the company holds a 1.42 percent stake in the NSE, which stands to benefit from the exchange’s potential listing.

title: NSE targets listing on Sep 25, reports CNBC-TV18; IFCI, NIACL shares rise up to 15%
